paragraphs: One-sentence judgment: biochemists and biophysicists are not people who produce pretty data with instruments, but research positions that take the chemical composition or physical principles of living cells and organisms as their object and write hypothesis, experimental design, data collection and analysis, and presentation of results into a reviewable chain of evidence: write papers or share research findings at conferences, mentor graduate students, develop new methods to study the mechanisms of biological processes, write grant proposals, design and conduct experiments using equipment such as lasers or accelerators or mass spectrometers, determine the three-dimensional structures of biological macromolecules, study the effects of substances such as drugs and hormones on tissues and life processes, develop or test new drugs intended for market, produce proteins for medicinal or industrial use using recombinant DNA techniques, and analyze biochemical or biophysical data; people who only want ready-made conclusions and are unwilling to trace the original data and control conditions, unwilling to work within the authorized level according to biosecurity and hazardous chemical rules, and unwilling to truthfully record and review uncertainty and negative results are not suited to it.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to trace a conclusion back to the original data and experimental conditions and instrument parameters; you can spend long periods at the bench and in front of instruments doing repeated measurements and keep the records consistent; when results do not match the hypothesis or the data are anomalous you are willing to review and record truthfully rather than selecting favorable data; you are willing to stop and report first when experimental activities or biosecurity levels exceed the approval or filing.

Conditions for pausing your investment first: you have not yet completed, under any supervised condition, one full closed loop of proposing a hypothesis, designing experiments and controls, collecting and recording raw data, analyzing and reviewing, and stating things truthfully, or you can only explain your interest by liking biology and chemistry; nor should you treat being able to operate a particular instrument or use a particular analysis software as proof that you can independently design high-risk experiments or independently handle experimental activities involving human genetic resources and pathogenic microorganisms. Biosecurity and experimental activity levels, the collection and preservation and external provision of pathogenic microorganisms and human genetic resources, the conditions for using hazardous chemicals, and the recording and preservation of research data must be carried out in accordance with the applicable jurisdiction and competent authorities and employer systems and must leave a traceable record; this page does not provide any experimental method, practice for circumventing regulation or criterion for determining biosecurity levels.

The employment projection is faster than average (5% to 6%; the employment trends page gives 35,600 people in 2024 → about 37,600 people in 2034, 6%, while still projecting about 2,900 openings per year on average over the projection period). At the same time it must be noted: the wage and employment and industry data on this page are all reported on a standalone basis for this occupation on the O*NET page (the page contains no Wage data for ... or Employment data for ... labels taken from other occupations). Education, post-doctoral training, industry certification, employer hiring and position authorization, and the requirements of the applicable jurisdiction for biosecurity and laboratories and hazardous chemicals and human genetic resources are different states and must be verified item by item according to employer and position and jurisdiction; none of them can be automatically inferred from another.

One sentence: this is a scientific position centered on hypotheses and experiments and data that delivers reviewable research conclusions through prolonged uncertainty and repeated verification; the core is experimental design and execution and data analysis and presentation of results and compliance, not the imagination of living phenomena; its U.S. wages and employment are reported on a standalone basis for this occupation, and the employment projection is faster than average; on the mainland China side no precise occupational wage entry has been obtained, and this page does not fill it in with industry averages or parent occupations or U.S. data.

The work of biochemists and biophysicists can be divided into three categories: experimental and research tasks (propose hypotheses and design experiments and controls; design or conduct experiments using equipment such as lasers or accelerators or mass spectrometers; determine the three-dimensional structure or spatial configuration of biological macromolecules such as proteins using X-rays or electron microscopes; design or build the experimental equipment needed for a specific research project; isolate and analyze or synthesize vitamins and hormones and allergens and minerals or enzymes and determine their effects on body functions; develop or carry out tests to detect diseases and genetic disorders or other abnormalities; develop or test new drugs intended for commercial launch and prepare medicinal compounds; produce proteins for medicinal or industrial use using recombinant DNA techniques); data and record and sample management (collect and record raw data and instrument parameters and reagent lots and control conditions; analyze biochemical or biophysical data; preserve samples and data and experimental records according to procedure and keep them traceable; update methods and parameters as needed); and result analysis and papers and external presentation (write scientific papers or present at academic conferences to share research findings; write reports or recommendations based on research results; write research grant proposals; mentor undergraduate or graduate students and supervise their research; manage a laboratory team or oversee the quality of the team's work). What the three categories share is writing hypothesis and conditions and data and judgment clearly, rather than taking the desired result first and adding the conditions afterwards.

O*NET occupational identity and tasks: O*NET 19-1021.00 Biochemists and Biophysicists (page updated in 2026, marked Bright Outlook). The official responsibility is to study the chemical composition or physical principles of living cells and organisms and their electrical and mechanical energy and related phenomena; the official tasks total 25 items (grouped into core tasks and supplemental tasks), with importance scores from 93 down to lower percentiles. Work activities are listed as 41 items on the detailed page with importance scores, the highest being analyzing data or information 99, documenting and recording information 94, thinking creatively 94, updating and using relevant knowledge 94, getting information 93, making decisions and solving problems 93, processing information 93, using computers 92, identifying objects and actions and events 89, interpreting the meaning of information for others 88, communicating with supervisors or peers or subordinates 84, monitoring processes and materials or surroundings 84, developing objectives and strategies 83, estimating quantifiable characteristics of products and events or information 83, training and teaching others 79, organizing and planning and prioritizing work 78, inspecting equipment and structures or materials 75, judging the qualities of objects and services or people 74, guiding and directing and motivating subordinates 71, and coaching and developing others 69; it also lists drafting and laying out and specifying technical devices and parts 53, handling and moving objects 44, resolving conflicts and negotiating with others 41, recruiting and selecting personnel 41, assisting and caring for others 40, selling or influencing others 40, repairing and maintaining mechanical equipment 39, performing general physical activities 34, operating vehicles and mechanical equipment 29, and working with the public or performing 24.

Conduct experiments and collect data | Give the data a source | Operate instruments and reagents according to procedure within the approved laboratory level and authorized scope, and record raw data and instrument parameters and reagent lots and control conditions by number.

Analyze data and review anomalies | Make the conclusion testable | Analyze data with public methods and reproducible processes, and review and re-measure anomalies and negative results first rather than taking only the parts you want.

Record and preserve samples and data | Make the process traceable | Preserve raw data and experimental records and samples according to institutional data management and sample management rules, and record methods and versions and manual handling traces.

Write and share results | Make the statement consistent with the evidence | Write papers and reports and grant proposals, truthfully state conclusions and uncertainty and limitations, and handle authorship and data sharing according to institutional rules.

Report and escalate | Make responsibility transferable | When experimental conditions do not comply or data are anomalous or biosecurity or human genetic resources or hazardous chemicals are involved or something is beyond your authorization, report and hand over according to the authorization chain and record truthfully, without relaxing conditions or handling it on your own.

paragraphs: All six directions share a foundation of experimentation and data and safety and compliance common sense, but the core objects, delivery results, external authority and authorization requirements differ; the same laboratory or analytical experience cannot be directly converted into the authorization or decision authority of another direction (for example, whether design and interpretation responsibility is borne and whether human genetic resources and pathogenic microorganisms are involved differ considerably), and this page only compares the differences in duties under public scope.

The basis for comparison is the official occupation description of O*NET 19-1021.00 and the list of related occupations on the O*NET page (Animal Scientists, Bioengineers and Biomedical Engineers, Bioinformatics Scientists, Chemists, Geneticists, Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technicians, Medical Scientists, Except Epidemiologists, Microbiologists, Molecular and Cellular Biologists, Physicists), as well as the adjacent occupation relationships noted in the routing materials; an adjacent relationship only indicates proximity of duties and does not mean that qualifications, authorization or positions are interchangeable.

The table below compares biochemists and biophysicists with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which choice suits each preference.

Data scientists deliver data and modeling and prediction as their main output and usually work in a computational environment; biochemists and biophysicists take the experiments and data of life processes as their main object and need to design and conduct experiments themselves and be responsible for their physical and chemical meaning.
If you would rather do modeling and data products and algorithm delivery, compare data scientists first; if you would rather generate and interpret data at the bench, then this occupation suits you.
Complete data processing and modeling and result delivery, with outputs mainly in models and data products and reports.
Biochemists and biophysicists and data scientists

Bioengineers and biomedical engineers deliver engineering design and devices or systems or processes, driven by engineering standards and product requirements; biochemists and biophysicists deliver mechanism discovery and reproducible experimental evidence, driven by scientific questions.

If you would rather do device and system or process design and verification, compare bioengineers and biomedical engineers first; if you would rather pursue mechanisms and evidence, then this occupation suits you.
Complete design and verification and engineering delivery, with outputs mainly in design schemes and devices or systems and verification reports.
Biochemists and biophysicists and bioengineers and biomedical engineers

Nanosystems engineers deliver the design and integration and engineering realization of nanoscale systems and lean toward engineering and manufacturing; biochemists and biophysicists study the structures and processes of biological molecules and lean toward basic mechanisms and experimental evidence.

If you would rather do nanoscale system design and integration, compare nanosystems engineers first; if you would rather study the structures and processes of biological molecules, then this occupation suits you.
Complete nanosystem design and integration, with outputs mainly in system schemes and devices and test results.
Biochemists and biophysicists and nanosystems engineers

Nanotechnology engineering technologists and technicians take on equipment operation and process execution and maintenance, with implementation according to procedure as their main duty; biochemists and biophysicists bear responsibility for hypothesis and design and interpretation and presentation.

If you would rather operate and maintain precision equipment and processes according to procedure, compare nanotechnology engineering technologists and technicians first; if you would rather bear design and interpretation responsibility, then this occupation suits you.
Complete equipment operation and process execution and maintenance records, with outputs mainly in operation and maintenance and test records.
Biochemists and biophysicists and nanotechnology engineering technologists and technicians

Animal scientists take animal production and nutrition and welfare and breeding as their main object and often work in agriculture and farming and veterinary related contexts; biochemists and biophysicists take the chemical and physical mechanisms at the molecular and cellular level as their main object.

If you would rather do animal production and nutrition and welfare and breeding, compare animal scientists first; if you would rather do mechanism research at the molecular and cellular level, then this occupation suits you.
Complete animal production and nutrition and breeding research, with outputs mainly in trial and feeding and breeding records and research conclusions.
Biochemists and biophysicists and animal scientists

Chemists take chemical substances and reactions and synthesis and analytical methods as their main object and mostly work in chemical and materials and industrial contexts; biochemists and biophysicists apply chemical and physical methods to living systems, and their object is living organisms and biological molecules.

If you would rather do substance synthesis and analytical methods and chemical processes, compare chemists first; if you would rather apply chemical and physical methods to living systems, then this occupation suits you.
Complete substance synthesis and analysis, with outputs mainly in synthetic routes and analytical methods and compound data.

Need to add training in computational methods and statistics and programming and data engineering; biochemical and biophysical experimental experience does not equal the ability to process and model large-scale sequence and omics data.
What is transferable is the foundation in molecular biology and experimental design and data analysis.

Need to add training in genetics and genomics and statistical genetics and pedigree and population analysis; biochemistry experience does not equal the variant and pedigree analysis ability of genetics research.
What is transferable is the foundation in molecular biology and experiments and data analysis.

Editorial comparison according to the tasks: both involve research at the molecular level, but the object shifts from chemical and physical processes to genes and hereditary mechanisms. It is not a measured transition distance, success rate or difficulty ranking.

Need to add training in microorganism culture and identification and biosecurity; biochemistry experience does not equal the culture and identification and biosecurity handling ability of microbiology research.
What is transferable is the foundation in aseptic technique and experiments and data recording.

Editorial comparison according to the tasks: both involve laboratory research, but the object and biosecurity requirements differ. It is not a measured transition distance, success rate or difficulty ranking.

Need to add training in disease mechanisms and clinical research and subject protection and drug regulation; biochemistry experience does not equal clinical research and ethics and regulatory ability.
What is transferable is the foundation in molecular mechanisms and experiments and data analysis.

Editorial comparison according to the tasks: both involve life science research, but the shift is from molecular mechanisms to the disease and clinical and population level. It is not a measured transition distance, success rate or difficulty ranking.

Need to add training in synthetic and analytical chemistry; applying chemical methods to living systems and taking chemical substances themselves as the research object differ in questions and outputs.
What is transferable is the foundation in chemistry and analytical methods and instruments.

What is transferable is the foundation in experimentation and measurement and data analysis.

entries.answer: Study the chemical composition or physical principles of living cells and organisms and their electrical and mechanical energy and related phenomena: write scientific papers or present at academic conferences to share research findings, mentor undergraduate or graduate students and supervise their research, apply methods from mathematics and physics and chemistry or biology to study the physical principles of living cells or organisms, manage a laboratory team or oversee the quality of the team's work, develop new methods to study the mechanisms of biological processes, write research grant proposals, design or conduct experiments using equipment such as lasers or accelerators or mass spectrometers, determine the three-dimensional structures of biological macromolecules, design or build the experimental equipment needed for a specific research project, and write reports or recommendations based on research results; and depending on the research direction, study the chemistry of processes such as cell development and respiration and digestion and the energy changes of growth and aging and death, study the mutations that cause cancer or other diseases, study the chemical effects of drugs and serum and hormones or food on tissues or life processes, use atomic isotopes to study the transformation of substances within cells, develop or carry out tests to detect diseases and genetic disorders or other abnormalities, develop or test new drugs intended for commercial launch, isolate and analyze or synthesize vitamins and hormones and allergens and minerals or enzymes and determine their effects on body functions, study the molecular or chemical aspects of immune system function, study how traits are passed from generation to generation, prepare medicinal compounds intended for commercial launch, develop methods for processing or storing or using food and drugs or compounds, study the nature and composition or expression of genes and how genetic engineering affects these processes, produce proteins for medicinal or industrial use using recombinant DNA techniques, and analyze biochemical or biophysical data.
entries.question: What do biochemists and biophysicists do every day?

entries.answer: Key risks include crossing experimental activity and biosecurity level boundaries, exposure to chemicals and biological agents and radiation, compliance of human genetic resources and biological samples and data, research integrity and the traceability of data and records, long experimental postures and repetitive actions and eye strain, and the external presentation of research results beyond authorization; the control approach is to work first within the approved or filed scope and carry out risk assessment, operate according to institutional procedures and wear the corresponding protection, truthfully record raw data and parameters and reagent lots and anomalies, handle samples and data and personal information on the principles of legality and propriety and necessity, and stop and escalate when beyond authorization or when anomalies are found.
entries.question: What risk does this job most need to note in advance?

entries.answer: Look at reviewable output: whether you can break a research question into testable hypotheses and design controls and sampling plans, whether you can collect and truthfully record raw data and instrument parameters and reagent lots according to procedure, and whether you can stop and review and report when data are anomalous or results do not match the hypothesis or something is beyond your authorization. An interest code of I and skill and knowledge scores only indicate that the direction is close and cannot replace this practical evidence.

entries.answer: AI and automation can change literature search and review compilation, data cleaning and statistics and visualization, sequence and structure prediction, and record organization and inventory and schedule management; but the judgment of experimental design and controls, the review of the usability of raw data and samples, the interpretation of anomalies and negative results, and disposition decisions on biosecurity and human genetic resources and hazardous chemicals are still borne by people. The degree of task automation does not equal a change in the number of positions; the official employment projection for this occupation is faster than average (6% for 2024 to 2034).

source_links.label: Law on the Safety of Hazardous Chemicals (effective 2026)
source_links.scope: China's Law on the Safety of Hazardous Chemicals takes effect on 2026-05-01, and Article 5 clarifies the responsibilities and training and assessment of user units such as schools and research institutions; Articles 46 through 51 require safety conditions, procedures, and Chinese-language safety data sheets and labels to be implemented according to type, hazardous characteristics, quantity and method. The safe use permit under Article 48 is aimed at chemical enterprises engaged in production with prescribed varieties and quantities, and not every research laboratory needs the same permit; radioactive substances and others follow their applicable rules separately, and waste disposal must also be verified separately against environmental protection provisions.

source_links.label: Personal Information Protection Law
source_links.scope: Personal information processing in China is checked against the Personal Information Protection Law for a lawful basis, necessity and security measures; identifiable personal medical health and the like are sensitive personal information with requirements for a specific purpose, sufficient necessity and strict protection. Not all scientific research data or non-human samples are sensitive personal information; human genetic resource rules and personal information rules should be judged separately, and foreign requirements cannot be replaced by Chinese provisions.

hero.quick_answer: Biochemists and biophysicists study the chemical composition or physical principles of living cells and organisms and their electrical and mechanical energy and related phenomena, and may conduct research to deepen understanding of the complex chemical combinations and reactions involved in metabolism and reproduction and growth and heredity, and may determine the effects of substances such as food and drugs and serum and hormones on tissues and life processes; common work includes writing scientific papers or presenting at academic conferences to share research findings, mentoring undergraduate or graduate students and supervising their research, applying methods and knowledge from mathematics and physics and chemistry or biology to study the physical principles of living cells or organisms, managing a laboratory team or overseeing the quality of the team's work, developing new methods to study the mechanisms of biological processes, writing research grant proposals, designing or conducting experiments using equipment such as lasers or accelerators or mass spectrometers, determining the three-dimensional structures of biological macromolecules, designing or building the experimental equipment needed for a specific research project, writing reports or recommendations based on research results, studying the spatial configuration of submicroscopic molecules such as proteins using X-rays or electron microscopes, studying the chemistry of life processes such as cell development and respiration and digestion and the energy changes of growth and aging and death, studying organism mutations that cause cancer or other diseases, studying the chemical effects of substances such as drugs and serum and hormones or food on tissues or life processes, using atomic isotopes to study the transformation of substances within cells, developing or carrying out tests to detect diseases and genetic disorders or other abnormalities, developing or testing new drugs intended for commercial launch, isolating and analyzing or synthesizing vitamins and hormones and allergens and minerals or enzymes and determining their effects on body functions, studying the molecular or chemical aspects of immune system function, studying how plant or animal traits are passed from generation to generation, preparing medicinal compounds intended for commercial launch, developing methods for processing or storing or using food and drugs or compounds, studying the nature and composition or expression of genes and how genetic engineering affects these processes, producing proteins for medicinal or industrial use using recombinant DNA techniques, and analyzing biochemical or biophysical data; their work does not equal clinical diagnosis and treatment decisions or conclusions on drug marketing authorization, nor does it replace the regulatory requirements of the applicable jurisdiction and competent authorities and employers for biosecurity and laboratories and hazardous chemicals and human genetic resource management, and it stops and escalates when experimental activities exceed the approved or filed scope or biosecurity level, when highly pathogenic pathogenic microorganisms and the collection and preservation and external provision of human genetic resources are involved, or when anomalies in data and records are found or situations beyond one's authorization are involved.

subject.name: Biochemists and biophysicists
subject.summary: Biochemists and biophysicists study the chemical composition or physical principles of living cells and organisms and their electrical and mechanical energy: share research findings, mentor graduate students, develop new methods to study the mechanisms of biological processes, write grant proposals, design and conduct experiments using equipment such as lasers or accelerators or mass spectrometers, determine the three-dimensional structures of biological macromolecules, study the chemical effects of substances such as drugs and hormones on tissues and life processes, develop or test new drugs intended for market, produce proteins for medicinal or industrial use using recombinant DNA techniques, and analyze biochemical or biophysical data. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET 19-1021.00 (Biochemists and Biophysicists), which is Job Zone Five (extensive preparation needed, mostly graduate-level education); O*NET marks this occupation as Bright Outlook; the wage and employment and industry data are all reported on a standalone basis for this occupation, and the page does not state that they are taken from other occupations; the employment projection is faster than average (5% to 6%; the employment trends page gives 35,600 people in 2024 → 37,600 people in 2034, 6%, with about 2,900 job openings per year on average). On the mainland China side, this page has not obtained a public occupational wage entry precisely corresponding to this occupation, and according to the evidence standard retains the boundary that no data can be safely used, without filling it in with industry averages, parent occupations or U.S. data; experimental and research activities in mainland China are subject to the Biosecurity Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on the Safety Administration of Hazardous Chemicals and other provisions.
